## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kuṭajapupphiyattheraapadāna* is a verse narrative preserved in the Therāpadāna section of the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. Following the standard structural conventions of the Apadāna, the poem details the meritorious deeds—specifically an offering associated with *kuṭaja* flowers—and subsequent spiritual attainments of the elder (thera) Kuṭajapupphiya across past and present lives [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral lists five translations of the text across five different languages [SuttaCentral].

Automated analysis by DharmaNexus identifies substantial formulaic text reuse within the Pali corpus, registering 88 matching passages across 28 texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest reuse correspondences appear in the Theragāthā commentary (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, both parts one and two), which shares extended passages with the apadāna (including segments §0.3–4.2 and §0.3–5.1) [DharmaNexus]. Additionally, standard thematic verses are shared with various other botanical offering narratives in the Therāpadāna, such as the *Ketakapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 516), *Nāgapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 517), *Campakapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 348), and *Sālamaṇḍapiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 492) [DharmaNexus]. A low-scoring machine alignment with the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99) reflects incidental phraseological similarity rather than an established textual parallel [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
